fieldValues.title: Engine bindings published on npm from promoted releases
fieldValues.decision_question: Should the engine's WASM bindings (srs-bindings) be published to the public npm registry, and if so, from every build or only from releases that pass the release gate?
fieldValues.context: The exercise 'Publish srs-bindings to npm' (6f3839be, checked 2026-11-06 against srs-rust 43b1ce8e) found that SP-79 (Third parties cannot install the engine as a library, affirmed) holds: srs-bindings ships only as a GitHub release tarball (srs-bindings-web.tar.gz), which srs-web fetches through scripts/ensure-bindings.mjs pinned to one build. srs-rust#819 (open) plans the publish from release.yml but leaves the package name ('@semanticops/srs-bindings, name TBD'), the pre-1.0 version policy and the publishing account open. The exercise set out three options: A, publish every build under an @semanticops scope as 0.<build>.0; B, publish only promoted releases, after the corpus gate (srs-rust#877), so npm's latest matches GitHub's latest; C, keep the tarball with a documented install recipe. The group's lean is Portability (decision 7270e772). As of 2026-11-10 srs-rust#877 ('the gate doesn't gate') is closed, and GitHub marks one release Latest (v0.1.0-build.641). A new public distribution channel is a contract the owner holds; Decision 0b1c25b1 requires a recorded ruling before the Third-party-ready group files a CLI, payload or WASM contract change; this record is that ruling.
fieldValues.friction: A third party cannot `npm install` the engine; they must find a release URL, download a tarball and pin it by hand, which is what SP-79 names, and srs-rust#819 cannot be promoted to ready work without a ruling.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: 1. Publish every build (option A): fastest feedback, but npm accumulates several versions a day, including builds the corpus gate would not promote, and third parties pick up drafts. 2. Publish only promoted releases (recommended, option B): release.yml publishes when a release passes the corpus gate and becomes Latest, versioned 0.<build>.0 under an owner-created @semanticops scope. Leads to: one meaning of 'latest' on both channels and a lower publish rate. 3. Keep the tarball and document an install recipe (option C): no account or token to hold, but SP-79 stays true in substance: no package manager resolution, no semver ranges. 4. Do nothing: srs-rust#819 stays blocked.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Portability (installable by a stranger with standard tools) against Reliability (one release channel, nothing to rotate). The published version must be no less checked than GitHub's Latest. Prerequisites the owner alone holds: creating the npm scope (proposed name @semanticops, package srs-bindings) and an automation token stored as an srs-rust environment secret; the ruling does not take effect until both exist. Pre-1.0, breaking changes may land in a minor version, as srs-rust#819 suggests. Out of scope: Node (non-web) builds and any other language registry. The exercise made no recommendation; the option chosen here is the drafter's proposal, for the owner to ratify, edit or set aside.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The engine's WASM bindings are published to the public npm registry from each release that passes the release gate, and from no other build.
fieldValues.rationale: SP-79 is about installability, and only a registry package solves it; the recipe in option C leaves the third party doing by hand what npm does. Tying publication to the gate keeps the registry from becoming a second, less-checked release channel, and the gate now works (srs-rust#877 closed), so the condition is enforceable.
fieldValues.revisit_when: The gated release rate is too slow for srs-web or a third party (they pin tarballs again to get fixes); or the token or scope becomes a maintenance burden (a rotation or a compromise); or a third-party integrator is found working comfortably from the tarball, which would make option C enough.
fieldValues.next_steps: After ratification: the owner creates the npm scope and token; srs-rust#819 is reshaped as Door 1 work under semanticops.com#31 and srs-web's pin move follows, as linked issues.
